 Leeds’ biggest food festival confirms 2027 dates for its best one yet
 Is it summer yet? 
Clementine Hall -
 28th October 2026 
 Organisers of The North Leeds Food Festival have confirmed the dates for their eleventh annual celebration . 
 Following an absolute belter of a milestone tenth anniversary, the beloved North Leeds Food Festival is gearing up to return to Roundhay Park. 
 The festival, which is the biggest food festival in Leeds, will take place on Saturday 8 and Sunday 9 May 2027. 
 And it's set to be the best one yet, as plans are already underway to build on a decade of celebrations, introducing an expanded entertainment programme, brand-new attractions and partnerships with hundreds of independent businesses from across Leeds and the wider Yorkshire region.
 Image: Supplied / Jack Biggins Photography 
 The ethos of the festival remains the same and lies in a celebration of international influence and community spirit expressed through street food, artisan markets, live entertainment, music, performing arts and charity. 
 Visitors can expect an expanded street food village, two independent bars, and an even bigger programme of events including live music, cooking demonstrations and family-friendly activities. 
 Image: Supplied / Jack Biggins Photography 
 Festival Director, Michael Johnston, said: “We’ve come a long way since our first event at Roundhay Park back in 2016. Celebrating our tenth anniversary this spring was incredibly special, and we owe it to the wonderful support we’ve received from the local community year after year. 
 "It’s not something we’ll ever take for granted. In testament to that, we want to keep building on what we’ve achieved together over the last ten years and continue to find new ways to elevate the experience for everyone who joins us.”
 Image: Supplied / Jack Biggins Photography 
 Assistant Festival Manager, Izaak Shuttleworth, added: “We want there to be something exciting for every person who walks through our doors, whether they’re joining us for the first time or returning each year."
 "Attendee feedback plays a huge role in how we develop the festival, and we’re working closely with new entertainers and independent businesses to bring some fresh ideas to life. We’re looking to create our most varied and interactive programme to date, so there’ll be plenty to look forward to next spring.”

 Leeds station to undergo £303m transformation in biggest upgrade for a generation
 Clementine Hall 
 Leeds train station set for biggest transformation in a generation as Government backs growth. 
 If you thought the work was over for Leeds station, think again. 
 Because passengers are set to see major improvements as the Government injects a further £200 million into the development of the transport hub.
 The additional funding was announced at the Budget today, with upgrades set to be delivered by 2030 and will include the construction of a new central overbridge, three new entrances, more space on the concourses and a longer Platform 14.
 Image: Supplied 
 It means passengers will benefit from more direct routes, less crowding, and nearly 40% more ticket barriers. 
 Three new entrances will strengthen links between the station and town, improving access to the South Bank, the Dark Arches and Princes Square. 
 Transport Secretary, Heidi Alexander, said: "Leeds station is the gateway to West Yorkshire, and this extra £200 million investment will turn it into a station this city can be proud of: modern, welcoming and built for the people who rely on it every single day. 
 "The great cities of the north deserve better transport, and that’s exactly what we’re delivering. We're paving the way for Northern Powerhouse Rail, forging stronger connections across the region, and backing the infrastructure that creates jobs, builds homes and puts passengers first as we work to set up Great British Railways."
 Mayor of West Yorkshire Tracy Brabin said: "Leeds Station is the beating heart of our region's transport network, connecting millions of people to jobs, education and opportunity every year – and it’s only going to get busier. 
 “This investment will benefit passengers and businesses, help to unlock the capacity we need for future growth and create a gateway to West Yorkshire that reflects our ambition. 
 “Together with our wider plans for West Yorkshire’s Weaver Network, we're building a better-connected region which works for all.”

 You can watch The Celebrity Traitors finale on a massive screen in Leeds this Friday
 Clementine Hall 
 The finale of The Celebrity Traitors is hitting our TV screens this Friday, and there’s a big screening party happening in Leeds especially for it. 
 Don't panic guys, it's happening.
 Fancy sitting down to watch one of the cultural events of the year on a big screen with dozens of others who are just as invested in the show as you are? Well, now you can.
 And that’s because Headrow House, one of the city’s most beloved event space, rooftop and bar, will be hosting a finale watching party - and we’re all invited.
 Taking place this Friday 30 October, fans of The Traitors are invited to watch the finale at 8pm.
 The best part? Entry is completely free and they'll even be streaming the semi-final ahead of the final at 6pm, so you can indulge in a double bill of the country's most beloved show.
 View this post on Instagram 
 A post shared by 🌿 HEADROW HOUSE 🌿 (@headrowhouse) 
 We honestly couldn't think of a better way to spend a Friday evening and we're already searching our wardrobes for an item of clothing that remotely resembles a cloak.
 Announcing the very exciting news to Instagram, Headrow House said: "celebrity traitors final this friday! we’ll be showing the semi-final for anyone who missed it before tuning in for the live final. free entry, get down early for a seat and bring your claudia wigs x"
 So to give this series of The Celebrity Traitors a proper send off, get yourself to Headrow House from 6pm and enjoy a few beverages with like minded fans whilst screaming at the screen as Claudia makes her way into the frame.
 Whilst we're on the topic, has anyone got an incredibly glossy black fringed wig we could borrow?
